  34|        The Monty Tech Cooperative Education Program is an extension of the student’s technical education that
  35|        combines classroom instruction with            on-the-job-training.  The                                                                                    popular Co           -op Program provides students
  36|        with an opportunity to further develop academic, technical and employability skills in an industry-                       related

===PAGE 126=== (layout, 41 lines)
   1| work environment. All students are eligible to participate in the Co           -op Program, provided they satisfy state
   2| and school grade, attendance and performance requirements, and all             Co           -op students must have completed the
   3| OSHA recognized Career Safe online health and safety course prior to being placed in a work environment.
   4| The Cooperative Education Program is beneficial for both students             and             employers.     For the student, it is a
   5| chance to gain on-the-job training                                                                                                                                                                    that             improves both their                                    technical proficiency             and             employability skills,
   6| and making industry connections enhances post-graduate employment opportunities.             The Co-op Program
   7| also allows students to earn while they learn, which has allowed many students to learn valuable life skills,
   8| financial literacy skills, and gain a deeper understanding of the importance of career advancement and self-
   9| advocacy.
  10| Employer benefits             include addressing workforce                                                            needs             in            an             efficient             manner.  Co            -op students provide a
  11| pool of trained talent, ready to assume temporary, part-time or even full-time opportunities, thus reducing
  12| employer training costs.   Co           -op work                                                             hours may also be tailored to suit the needs of partnering employers.
  13| With approximately 100 area employers participating in Cooperative Education, providing valuable
  14| experience to 286 students by the end of the                                                                                                2024/2025 school year, school officials remain grateful for their
  15| continued support, and look forward to future collaborations.

  17| oversees special education programming, and maintains efforts to provide social/emotional learning and
  18| resources to all students.              Throughout the 2025-                                                                                                    2026 school year, department staff continued to prioritize the
  19| district's effort to educate and develop the next generation
  20| of young adults, ensuring students have access to support in
  21| academic and vocational programming, as well as services
  22| related to social and emotional wellness.
  23| Throughout an individual's high school career, Monty Tech
  24| offers numerous opportunities and support for individuals
  25| to explore vocational interests, develop skills, and make
  26| strides in personal growth and independence.              All students
  27| establish goals and identify pathway interests that align
  28| with DESE’s MyCAP (My Career and Academic Plan)

  30| work to provide structured support for students as they
  31| acclimate to the demands, pace and rigor of high school
  32| academics, vocational programming and extracurricular activities.
  33| Balancing curriculum and course pathways with current social norms, Monty Tech recognizes young adults
  34| are growing up in a world that is rapidly changing.              With increased exposure to technology and social media,
  35| the means in which young adults communicate and connect has shifted.                               With that, the foundational skills
  36| and social norms have also changed, taking on an array of variances that schools must recognize and address
  37| to effectively prepare students to be successful young adults.
  38| Recognizing the shift in experiences and brain development, Monty Tech has focused support on the
  39| growing concerns and struggles with age-appropriate interactions, use of social media, and the need for
  40| meaningful connections. The Department of Student Support has concentrated its efforts on creating a safe
  41| and supportive environment, offering opportunities and experiences that challenge our students to reflect,

  11| southern Massachusetts, where they engaged in team-building activities and challenged their mental and
  12| physical capabilities through obstacle courses and squad competitions. This four-day camp fostered
  13| camaraderie and leadership development with cadets from other JROTC programs in New England.
  14| Additionally, cadets supported three community 5K runs, including the Friends of Fitchburg Veterans 5K,
  15| the Rock and Roll 5K at Wachusett Brewery, and the Heroes Live Forever 5K. They provided assistance
  16| with parking, run route coordination, and vendor support. Participation in the annual Blacksmith Festival in
  17| Fitchburg, MA, offered them insights into community volunteerism and the craft of blacksmithing.
  18| In collaboration with the Fitchburg Salvation Army, cadets participated as bell ringers and conducted
  19| volunteer tolls, successfully collecting over $25,000 in donations to support the less fortunate in the Monty
  20| Tech community. This fundraising goes on to assist with the costs associated with clothing, housing, food,
  21| and transportation requirements for numerous community members.
  22| The Monty Tech Color Guard supported in excess of 25 color guards at numerous events, including Monty

===PAGE 129=== (layout, 39 lines)
   1| Tech home football games, community, and veteran ceremonies, as well as graduate and undergraduate
   2| celebrations at Fitchburg State University.
   3| A special Veterans Day ceremony on November 10th honored Monty Tech staff and student veteran family
   4| members through a collage display and sword detail presentation. Also, on November 10th, the MCJROTC
   5| celebrated the 250th birthday of the United States Marine Corps with a Birthday Ball. Over 250 cadets and
   6| guests attended for a four-course meal, music, and dancing.
   7| Cadets have also participated in several different competitions including National Marksmanship
   8| competitions, cyber- security competitions, and numerous Raider challenges with an emphasis on confidence
   9| and discipline.

  11| community outreach and volunteerism, as well as team building and small unit leadership development.
  12|                                  In recent years, the Mont       y Tech School of Continuing Education, has received
  13|                                  more than $2.7M in funding from Commonwealth Corporation, to provide
  14|                                  valuable workforce training at no-                                                          cost for individuals who may be unemployed or
  15|                                  underemployed.  These grant-funded training opportunities are an example of the
  16|                                  collaboration between the MassHire Workforce Investment Board, MassHire
  17|                                  North Central Career Center, the Executive Office of Labor and Workforce
  18|                                  Development, and generous sponsorship from Commonwealth Corporation,
  19|                                  making it possible for Monty Tech to offer meaningful job readiness training
  20|                                  in occupations with high demand and self-sustaining wages.
  21| In 2024-                                                                     2025, school leaders were pleased to offer 200-                                                      hour training programs in Automotive Collision
  22| Repair, Carpentry, Plumbing, and HVAC to qualified participants.  Of the 64 students who enrolled, 56
  23| participants persisted in completing their selected training program.  Of those, 21 having since secured full-
  24| time employment in their chosen occupations.              In addition to these grant-funded opportunities, the School of
  25| Continuing Education, continues to offer the area’s most affordable and comprehensive cosmetology training
  26| program, effectively preparing participants to sit for the Massachusetts State Board examinations.              In FY25,
  27| nine cosmetology students graduated from the program.
  28| Serving more than 1,700 community members annually, the School of Continuing Education is proud to
  29| offer training to a non-traditional student population, while working to develop new and important
  30| relationships with business partners in need of a talented candidate pool.              The Continuing Education staff
  31| understands that the strength of any vocational training program is dependent upon mutually beneficial
  32| relationships between the school and our business partners, and they work tirelessly to build relationships
  33| throughout the year.              In May 2025, the School of Continuing Education hosted the annual Job Fair,
  34| welcoming more than thirty area employers who spent time visiting with both day and evening students
  35| seeking job opportunities.              Numerous students attended the event, presented resumes to business
  36| representatives, and made contacts with employers that led to a first-time job placement and entry into the
  37| trades. Additionally, the School of Continuing Education hosted its first annual Fall and Spring Open
  38| Houses, designed to offer prospective students the opportunity to learn more about training programs, meet
  39| instructors and ask questions.

   1| The Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical School Practical Nursing Program class of 2025 achieved
   2| a remarkable 93% NCLEX-PN Pass Rate on their first attempt, exceeding the national first-           time pass rate of
   3| 86.6% for U.S.-      educated Practical Nursing candidates.  This achievement highlights the hard work and
   4| commitment of our students, along with the ongoing support and guidance from our faculty and staff.
   5| Our success starts with a learning environment that is supportive, student-focused, and built to help students
   6| grow into confident, capable nurses. Our faculty play a key role—not only teaching in the classroom and
   7| clinical setting but also mentoring students throughout the program. Coursework and clinical training are
   8| designed to strengthen clinical judgment and build a solid understanding of nursing practice. We emphasize
   9| evidence-based practice, critical thinking, patient safety, and compassionate, culturally aware care.
  10| We also know that student success includes more than academics. The program offers strong student support
  11| services, including academic advising, wellness resources, and assistance navigating financial assistance.
  12| Faculty advisors work closely with students, providing consistent encouragement and mentorship from day
  13| one through graduation.
  14| To continue expanding clinical learning opportunities, we are actively building new community clinical
  15| partnerships to give students experience in a variety of healthcare environments. These efforts support our
  16| goal of growing the program and preparing Practical Nurses who are ready to meet workforce needs across
  17| North Central Massachusetts.
  18| Ongoing improvement is a priority for our program. We regularly review and update our curriculum, invest
  19| in faculty development, and expand student resources to support learning and licensure success. We will
  20| continue incorporating technology and evidence-based teaching strategies to help students graduate prepared
  21| and career-ready.
  22| Community interest in the program remains strong, with more than 150 inquiries each year for 48 available
  23| seats in our annual cohort.

  24| ARTICLE 30.     To see if the Town will vote to amend the Code of Lunenburg, Chapter 250, being the
  25| Town’s “Protective Bylaw,” Article IV, entitled “Use Regulations,” by deleting therefrom in its entirety Section
  26| 4.8, entitled “Floodplain District,” and by substituting the following therefor:
  27| § 250-4.8.  Floodplain District.
  28| A.             The purpose of the Floodplain Overlay District is to:
  29|     (1)   Ensure public safety through reducing the threats to life and personal injury
  30|     (2)   Eliminate new hazards to emergency response officials
  31|     (3)   Prevent the occurrence of public emergencies resulting from water quality, contamination, and pollution
  32|          due to flooding
  33|     (4)   Avoid the loss of utility services which if damaged by flooding would disrupt or shut down the utility
  34|          network and impact regions of the community beyond the site of flooding
  35|     (5)   Eliminate costs associated with the response and cleanup of flooding conditions
  36|     (6)   Reduce damage to public and private property resulting from flooding water.
  37| B.                        Zone
  38| The Floodplain District is herein established as an overlay district.  The District includes all special flood hazard
  39| areas within Lunenburg designated as Zone A and AE on the Worcester County Flood Insurance Rate Map
  40| (FIRM) dated July 8, 2025 issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) for the
  41| administration of the National Flood Insurance Program.  The exact boundaries of the District shall be defined
  42| by the 1%-chance base flood elevations shown on the FIRM and further defined by the Worcester County Flood
  43| Insurance Study (FIS) report dated July 8, 2025.  The FIRM and FIS report are incorporated herein by reference
  44| and are on file with the Town Clerk, Planning Board, Building Official and Conservation Commission.
  45| C.                Definitions

===PAGE 144=== (layout, 43 lines)
   1| DEVELOPMENT means any man-made change to improved or unimproved real estate, including but not
   2| limited to building or other structures, mining, dredging, filling, grading, paving, excavation or drilling
   3| operations or storage of equipment or materials.
   4| FLOODWAY. The channel of the river, creek or other watercourse and the adjacent land areas that must be
   5| reserved in order to discharge the base flood without cumulatively increasing the water surface elevation more
   6| than a designated height.
   7| FUNCTIONALLY DEPENDENT USE means a use which cannot perform its intended purpose unless it is
   8| located or carried out in close proximity to water. The term includes only docking facilities, port facilities that
   9| are necessary for the loading and unloading of cargo or passengers, and ship building and ship repair facilities,
  10| but does not include long-term storage or related manufacturing facilities.
  11| HIGHEST ADJACENT GRADE means the highest natural elevation of the ground surface prior to construction
  12| next to the proposed walls of a structure.
  13| HISTORIC STRUCTURE means any structure that is:
  14| (a)            Listed individually in the National Register of Historic Places (a listing maintained by the Department of
  15|     Interior) or preliminarily determined by the Secretary of the Interior as meeting the requirements for
  16|     individual listing on the National Register;
  17| (b)       Certified or preliminarily determined by the Secretary of the Interior as contributing to the historical
  18|     significance of a registered historic district or a district preliminarily determined by the Secretary to qualify
  19|     as a registered historic district;
  20| (c)           Individually listed on a state inventory of historic places in states with historic preservation programs which
  21|     have been approved by the Secretary of the Interior; or
  22| (d)       Individually listed on a local inventory of historic places in communities with historic preservation
  23|     programs that have been certified either:
  24|     (1)   By an approved state program as determined by the Secretary of the Interior or
  25|     (2)   Directly by the Secretary of the Interior in states without approved programs.
  26| NEW CONSTRUCTION. Structures for which the start of construction commenced on or after the effective
  27| date of the first floodplain management code, regulation, ordinance, or standard adopted by the authority having
  28| jurisdiction, including any subsequent improvements to such structures. New construction includes work
  29| determined to be substantial improvement.
  30| RECREATIONAL VEHICLE means a vehicle which is:
  31| (e)           Built on a single chassis;
  32| (f)               400 square feet or less when measured at the largest horizontal projection;
  33| (g)          Designed to be self-propelled or permanently towable by a light duty truck; and
  34| (h)       Designed primarily not for use as a permanent dwelling but as temporary living quarters for recreational,
  35|     camping, travel, or seasonal use.
  36| REGULATORY FLOODWAY - The channel of the river, creek or other watercourse and the adjacent land
  37| areas that must be reserved in order to discharge the base flood without cumulatively increasing the water
  38| surface elevation more than a designated height.
  39| SPECIAL FLOOD HAZARD AREA. The land area subject to flood hazards and shown on a Flood Insurance
  40| Rate Map or other flood hazard map as Zone A, AE, A1-30, A99, AR, AO, AH.
  41| START OF CONSTRUCTION. The date of issuance for new construction and substantial improvements to
  42| existing structures, provided the actual start of construction, repair, reconstruction, rehabilitation, addition,
  43| placement or other improvement is within 180 days after the date of issuance. The actual start of construction

===PAGE 145=== (layout, 44 lines)
   1| means the first placement of permanent construction of a building (including a manufactured home) on a site,
   2| such as the pouring of a slab or footings, installation of pilings or construction of columns.  Permanent
   3| construction does not include land preparation (such as clearing, excavation, grading or filling), the installation
   4| of streets or walkways, excavation for a basement, footings, piers or foundations, the erection of temporary
   5| forms or the installation of accessory buildings such as garages or sheds not occupied as dwelling units or not
   6| part of the main building. For a substantial improvement, the actual “start of construction” means the first
   7| alteration of any wall, ceiling, floor or other structural part of a building, whether or not that alteration affects
   8| the external dimensions of the building.
   9| STRUCTURE means, for floodplain management purposes, a walled and roofed building, including a gas or
  10| liquid storage tank, that is principally above ground, as well as a manufactured home.
  11| SUBSTANTIAL REPAIR OF A FOUNDATION. When work to repair or replace a foundation results in the
  12| repair or replacement of a portion of the foundation with a perimeter along the base of the foundation that
  13| equals or exceeds 50% of the perimeter of the base of the foundation measured in linear feet, or repair or
  14| replacement of 50% of the piles, columns or piers of a pile, column or pier supported foundation, the building
  15| official shall determine it to be substantial repair of a foundation. Applications determined by the building
  16| official to constitute substantial repair of a foundation shall require all existing portions of the entire building or
  17| structure to meet the requirements of 780 CMR.
  18| VARIANCE means a grant of relief by a community from the terms of a flood plain management regulation.
  19| VIOLATION means the failure of a structure or other development to be fully compliant with the community's
  20| flood plain management regulations. A structure or other development without the elevation certificate, other
  21| certifications, or other evidence of compliance required in §60.3 is presumed to be in violation until such time
  22| as that documentation is provided.
  23| D.   Use Regulations.
  24| (1)   The Floodplain District is established as an overlay district to all other districts. All development, including
  25|      structural and nonstructural activities, must be in compliance with MGL c. 131, § 40 and with the
  26|      requirements of the Massachusetts State Building Code pertaining to construction in the floodplain.
  27| (2)   Permitted Uses. The following uses of low flood damage potential and causing no obstructions to flood
  28|      flows shall be allowed, provided they are permitted in the underlying district and they do not require
  29|      structures, fill or storage of materials or equipment:
  30|     (a)                                    Agricultural uses such as farming, grazing, truck farming, horticulture, etc.
  31|     (b)                               Forestry and nursery uses.
  32|     (c)                                   Outdoor recreational uses, including fishing, boating, play areas, etc.
  33|     (d)                               Conservation of water, plants, wildlife.
  34|     (e)                                   Wildlife management areas, foot, bicycle and/or horse paths.
  35|     (f)                                       Temporary nonresidential structures used in connection with fishing, growing, harvesting, storage or
  36|            sale of crops raised on the premises.
  37|     (g)                                  Buildings lawfully existing prior to the effective date hereof.
  38| (3) Uses permissible by special permit granted by the Planning Board. No structure or building                           shall be
  39|     erected, constructed, substantially improved or otherwise created or moved, no earth or other materials
  40|     dumped, filled, excavated or transferred, unless a special permit is granted by the Planning Board. Said
  41|     Board may issue a special permit hereunder, subject to other applicable provisions of this bylaw, if the
  42|     application is in compliance with the following provisions:
  43|     (a)                                    The proposed use shall comply in all respects with the provisions of the underlying district; and
  44|     (b)                               Within 10 days of receipt of the application, the Board shall transmit one copy of the development plan

===PAGE 146=== (layout, 39 lines)
   1|            to the Conservation Commission, Board of Health and Building Commissioner. Final action shall not
   2|            be taken until reports have been received from the above boards or until 35 days have elapsed; and
   3|     (c)                                   All encroachments, including fill, new construction, substantial improvements to existing structures
   4|            and other development, are prohibited unless certification by a registered professional engineer is
   5|            provided by the applicant demonstrating that such encroachment shall not result in any increase in
   6|            flood levels during the occurrence of the one-hundred-year flood; and
   7|     (d)                               The Board may specify such additional requirements and conditions it finds necessary to protect the
   8|            health, safety and welfare of the public and the occupant of the proposed use.
   9| E.                                     Designation of Community Floodplain Administrator
  10| The Town hereby designates the position of Building Commissioner to be the official floodplain administrator
  11| for the Town.
  12| F.                                        Special Permits are required for all proposed development in the Floodplain District
  13| The Town requires a special permit for all proposed construction or other development in the Floodplain
  14| District, including new construction or changes to existing buildings, placement of manufactured homes,
  15| placement of agricultural facilities, fences, sheds, storage facilities or drilling, mining, paving and any other
  16| development that might increase flooding or adversely impact flood risks to other properties.
  17| G.   Assure That All Necessary Permits Are Obtained
  18| The Town’s special permit review process includes the requirement that the proponent obtain all local, state and
  19| federal permits that will be necessary in order to carry out the proposed development in the Floodplain District.
  20| The proponent must acquire all necessary permits.
  21| H.              Floodway Encroachment
  22| In Zones A and AE, along watercourses that have not had a regulatory floodway designated, the best available
  23| Federal, State, local, or other floodway data shall be used to prohibit encroachments in floodways which would
  24| result in any increase in flood levels within the community during the occurrence of the base flood discharge.
  25| In Zone  AE, along watercourses that have a regulatory floodway designated on the Town’s FIRM,
  26| encroachments are prohibited, including fill, new construction, substantial improvements, and other
  27| development within the adopted regulatory floodway unless it has been demonstrated through hydrologic and
  28| hydraulic analyses performed in accordance with standard engineering practice that the proposed encroachment
  29| would not result in any increase in flood levels within the community during the occurrence of the base flood
  30| discharge.
  31| I.                                  Unnumbered A Zones
  32| In A Zones, in the absence of FEMA BFE data and floodway data, the Building Department will obtain, review
  33| and reasonably utilize base flood elevation and floodway data available from a Federal, State, or other source as
  34| criteria for requiring new construction, substantial improvements, or other development in Zone A and as the
  35| basis for elevating residential structures to or above base flood level, for floodproofing or elevating
  36| nonresidential structures to or above base flood level, and for prohibiting encroachments in floodways.
  37| J.    Subdivision proposals
  38| All subdivision proposals and development proposals in the Floodplain District shall be reviewed to assure that:
  39| (a)            Such proposals minimize flood damage.

===PAGE 147=== (layout, 39 lines)
   1| (b)       Public utilities and facilities are located & constructed so as to minimize flood damage.
   2| (c)           Adequate drainage is provided.
   3| K.                                Base flood elevation data for subdivision proposals
   4| When proposing subdivisions or other developments greater than 50 lots or 5 acres (whichever is less), the
   5| proponent must provide technical data to determine base flood elevations for each developable parcel shown on
   6| the design plans.
   7| L.                                     Recreational Vehicles
   8| In A and AE Zones, all recreational vehicles to be placed on a site must be elevated and anchored in accordance
   9| with the zone’s regulations for foundation and elevation requirements or be on the site for less than 180
  10| consecutive days or be fully licensed and highway ready.
  11| M.                        Watercourse alterations or relocations in riverine areas
  12| In a riverine situation, the Building Commissioner shall notify the following of any alteration or relocation of a
  13| watercourse:
  14| •                                                                                                                Adjacent Communities, especially upstream and downstream
  15| •                                                                                                                Bordering States, if affected
  16| •                                                                                                                NFIP State Coordinator
  17|                                                                                                                                                                                                              Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
  18| •                                                                                                                NFIP Program Specialist
  19|                                                                                                                                                       Federal Emergency Management Agency, Region I
  20| N.                                Requirement to Submit New Technical Data
  21| If the Town acquires data that changes the base flood elevation in the FEMA mapped Special Flood Hazard
  22| Areas, the Town will, within 6 months, notify FEMA of these changes by submitting the technical or scientific
  23| data that supports the change(s). Notification shall be submitted to:
  24| •                                                                                                                NFIP State Coordinator
  25|                                                                                                                                                                                                              Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
  26| •                                                                                                                NFIP Program Specialist
  27|                                                                                                                                                                                                   Federal Emergency Management Agency, Region I
  28| O.   Variances to Building Code Floodplain Standards
  29| The Town will request from the State Building Code Appeals Board a written and/or audible copy of the portion
  30| of the hearing related to the variance, and will maintain this record in the community’s files.
  31| The Town shall also issue a letter to the property owner regarding potential impacts to the annual premiums for
  32| the flood insurance policy covering that property, in writing over the signature of a community official that (i)
  33| the issuance of a variance to construct a structure below the base flood level will result in increased premium
  34| rates for flood insurance up to amounts as high as $25 for $100 of insurance coverage and (ii) such construction
  35| below the base flood level increases risks to life and property.
  36| Such notification shall be maintained with the record of all variance actions for the referenced development in
  37| the Floodplain District.
  38| P.                                        Variances to the Zoning Bylaw related to community compliance with the National Flood Insurance
  39|                      Program (NFIP)

===PAGE 148=== (layout, 38 lines)
   1| A variance from this Bylaw must meet the requirements set out by State law, and may only be granted if:

  29| ARTICLE 13.  MBTA ZONING ACT COMPLIANCE
  30| (Submitted by Planning Board)
  31| To see if the Town will vote to amend the Code of Lunenburg, Chapter 250, being the Town’s “Protective
  32| Bylaw,” so as to bring it into compliance with the MBTA Communities Act, being M.G.L. Chapter 40A,
  33| Section 3A, by adding a new Section 4.19 thereto, entitled “Multi-family Overlay District,” as follows:
  34| Section 250-4.19 Multi-family Overlay District.
  35| A.                                                                           Purpose
  36| The purpose of the Multi-family Overlay District (MOD) is to allow multi-                                family housing at a density of 26.1
  37| units per acre as of right per Section 3A of the Zoning Act (Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40A). This
  38| zoning provides for as of right multi-family housing to accomplish the following purposes:
  39|           1.                                                                             Promote public health, safety and welfare by encouraging the production of various housing
  40|           sizes and types to provide equal access to new housing throughout the community to meet the various

===PAGE 155=== (layout, 36 lines)
   1|             needs for people and households of all incomes, ages and sizes.
   2|             2.                                                                               Preserve open space in a community by locating new housing within or adjacent to existing
   3|             developed areas and infrastructure.
   4|             3.                                                                                                 Increase the municipal tax base through private investment in new residential developments.
   5| B.                                                                             Establishment and Applicability
   6| This MOD is an overlay district superimposed over the underlying zoning district and is shown on the Zoning
   7| Map.
   8|             1.                                                                                                 Underlying Zoning. The MOD is an overlay district superimposed on underlying zoning districts.
   9|             The regulations for use, dimension, and all other provisions of the Zoning Bylaw governing the
  10|             respective underlying zoning district(s) shall remain in full force, except for uses allowed as of right in
  11|             the MOD. Uses not identified in Section 250-                                                                                     4.19 are governed by the underlying zoning district(s)
  12|             requirements.
  13|             2.                                                                    Density Protection. The Planning Board shall have the authority to modify any conflicting
  14|             dimensional or design standards imposed by other sections of the zoning by-law if such standards would
  15|             result in a reduction of the base density of 26.1 units per acre for multifamily housing within the MOD.
  16| C.                                                                           Definitions.
  17| For Section 250-                                                                                               4.19, the following definitions shall apply. See Section 250-                                                 2 of the Zoning By-                laws for all
  18| other definitions.
  19|             1.                                                                                          Affordable unit. A multi-family housing unit that is subject to a use restriction recorded in its
  20|             chain of title limiting the sale price or rent or limiting occupancy to an individual or household of a
  21|             specified income, or both.
  22|             2.                                                                                                           Affordable housing. Housing that contains Affordable Units eligible for listing in the EOHLC’s
  23|             Subsidized Housing Inventory.
  24|             3.                                                   Applicant. A person, business, or organization that applies for a building permit, Site Plan
  25|             Review, or Special Permit.
  26|             4.                                                                        Area Median Income (AMI). The median family income for the Fitchburg-            Leominster, MA
  27|             statistical region includes the Town of Lunenburg as defined by the U.S. Department of Housing and
  28|             Urban Development (HUD).
  29|             5.                                                                                 As of right. Development that may proceed under the Zoning in place at the time of application
  30|             without needing a special permit, variance, zoning amendment, waiver, or other discretionary zoning
  31|             approval.

   5|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Minimum Rear Yard: 25 feet
   6|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Maximum Height: 38 feet
   7|                               Minimum Open Space: At least 10% of the total site area shall be devoted to open space;
   8|                               required setbacks shall be considered as part of the total area required for open space. The
   9|                               required open space shall not be used for parking or loading purposes and shall be open and
  10|                               unobstructed to the sky. Items such as benches, walkways, planters, landscaping, kiosks, gazebos

  13|                3.                                                Exceptions. The limitation on height of buildings shall not apply to chimneys, ventilators,

  15|                living purposes and do not constitute more than 25% of the ground floor area of the building.

  17| Multifamily development in the MOD shall provide two parking spaces per dwelling unit. Stand-                                         alone Parking
  18| Structures are prohibited.
  19| G.                                                                        General Development Standards
  20|                1.                                                Development standards in the MOD are applicable to all multi-              family and mixed-use
  21|                development. These standards are components of the Site Plan Review process in Section 250-4.19.J.
  22|                Site Plan Review.
  23|                2.                                                                                                                                     Site Design.
  24|                               a.                                                                                          Connections. Sidewalks shall provide direct connections among building entrances, the
  25|                               public sidewalk (if applicable), bicycle storage, and parking.
  26|                               b.                                                               Vehicular Access. Where feasible, curb cuts shall be minimized, and shared driveways
  27|                               encouraged.
  28|                               c.                                                                                                Screening for Parking. Surface parking adjacent to a public sidewalk shall be screened by
  29|                               a landscaped buffer of sufficient width to allow the healthy establishment of trees, shrubs, and
  30|                               perennials, but no less than 6 (six) feet. The buffer may include a fence or wall of no more than
  31|                               three feet in height unless there is a significant grade change between the parking and the
  32|                               sidewalk.
  33|                               d.                                                           Parking Materials. The parking surface may be concrete, asphalt, decomposed granite,
  34|                               bricks, or pavers, including pervious materials but not including grass or soil not contained
  35|                               within a paver or other structure. Pervious materials are encouraged.
  36|                               e.                                                                     Open Space and Plantings. Plantings shall include species that are native or adapted to
  37|                               the region. Plants on the Massachusetts Prohibited Plant List, as may be amended, shall be
  38|                               prohibited.

===PAGE 158=== (layout, 41 lines)
   1|            f.                                                                   Lighting. All exterior lighting shall be Dark Sky–compliant, employing fully shielded,
   2|            full-cutoff LED luminaires and meeting current Illuminating Engineering Society (IES) design
   3|            recommendations for the intended use; fixtures shall be mounted and aimed to prevent glare,
   4|            light trespass onto adjoining properties, and skyglow, and shall utilize controls (timers, dimming
   5|            and/or motion sensors) to reduce illumination outside operating hours.
   6|            g.                                                                                                        Mechanicals. Mechanical equipment at ground level shall be screened by a combination
   7|            of fencing and plantings. Rooftop mechanical equipment shall be screened if visible from a
   8|            public right-of-way.
   9|            h.                                                                            Dumpsters. Outdoor dumpsters will be enclosed on all sides by a building, fence, and/or
  10|            wall that has a landscaping buffer on at least 2 of the non-gated sides.
  11|            i.                                                       Stormwater Management. Strategies that demonstrate compliance of the construction
  12|            activities and the proposed project with the most current versions of the Massachusetts
  13|            Department of Environmental Protection Stormwater Management Standards, the Massachusetts
  14|            Stormwater Handbook, Massachusetts Erosion Sediment and Control Guidelines, the Town’s
  15|            Stormwater Bylaw, as amended, and, if applicable, additional requirements under the Town of
  16|            Lunenburg MS4 permit.
  17| 3.                                                                                                 Buildings: Multiple Buildings on a Lot.
  18|            a.                                                                                                                           Parking and circulation on the site shall be organized to reduce the amount of impervious
  19|            surface. Where possible, parking and loading areas shall be connected to minimize curb cuts onto
  20|            public rights-of-way. The minimum horizontal distance between any two curb cuts on the same
  21|            lot shall be no less than 100 feet.
  22|            b.                                                                       A paved pedestrian network shall connect parking to the entries to all buildings and the
  23|            buildings to each other and all walkways and connections shall meet accessibility standards.
  24|            c.                                                                   The orientation of multiple buildings on a lot should reinforce the relationships among
  25|            the buildings. All building façade(s) shall be treated with the same care and attention in terms of
  26|            entries, fenestration, and materials. The relationship of the buildings to the site, including the
  27|            siting of buildings, structures and open spaces, shall be designed to permit passive solar energy
  28|            and to permit maximum protection of pedestrian areas from adverse impact of winds, vapors or
  29|            other emissions, shadows and/or noise. The minimum horizontal distance between any two
  30|            principal buildings on the same lot shall be no less than 40 feet.
  31|            d.                                                   The building(s) adjacent to the public street shall have a pedestrian entry facing the
  32|            public street.
  33| 4.                                                                                                    Buildings: Shared Outdoor Space. Multi-family housing shall have common outdoor space that
  34| all residents can access. Such space may be in any combination of the courtyard, rooftop, or terrace.
  35| 5.                                                                           Buildings: Principal Façade and Parking. Parking shall be subordinate in design and location to
  36| the principal building façade while minimizing the extent of impervious surface. Vehicular parking
  37| spaces and garage doors shall be located behind the primary plane of the principal building façade.
  38|            a.                                                       Surface Parking. Surface parking shall be located at the rear or side of the principal
  39|            building. For the purposes of this section, a side location must be behind the primary plane of the
  40|            principal building façade and must be screened from the public right-of-way by landscaping or
  41|            fencing. Parking shall not be located in the required front setback between the building and any

===PAGE 159=== (layout, 36 lines)
   1|                          lot line adjacent to the public right-of-             way.
   2|                          b.                                                       Integrated Garages. Garage doors for residential units are prohibited on any principal
   3|                          façade that faces a public street. Integrated garages are permitted on a side or rear façade,
   4|                          including garage doors for ramps to underground parking.

   6|             Regulations, the Site Plan Review Authority may waive the requirements of this Section 250-4.19.G.

   8| H. Affordability Requirements.
   9|             1.                                                                                                 Purpose.
  10|                          a.                                                                           Promote the public health, safety, and welfare by encouraging a diversity of housing
  11|                          opportunities for people of different income levels;
  12|                          b.                                                                                              Provide for a full range of housing choices for households of all incomes, ages, and sizes;
  13|                          c.                                                   Increase the production of affordable housing units to meet existing and anticipated
  14|                          housing needs; and
  15|                          d.                                              Work to overcome economic segregation allowing the Town of Lunenburg to be a
  16|                          community of opportunity in which low and moderate-income households have the opportunity
  17|                          to advance economically.
  18|             2.                                                                                                                  Applicability. This requirement is applicable to all residential and mixed-use developments with
  19|             2 or more dwelling units, whether new construction, substantial rehabilitation, expansion,
  20|             reconstruction, or residential conversion. No project may be divided or phased to avoid the requirements
  21|             of this section.
  22|             3.                                                                                 Affordability requirements. Subsidized Housing Inventory: All units affordable to households
  23|             earning 80% or less of AMI created in the MOD under this section must be eligible for listing on
  24|             EOHLC’s Subsidized Housing Inventory.
  25|             4.                                                                                                                      Provision of Affordable Housing. In Applicable Projects, 10% of housing units constructed shall
  26|             be Affordable Housing Units. For purposes of calculating the number of units of Affordable Housing
  27|             required within a development project, a fractional unit shall be rounded down to the next whole
  28|             number. The Affordable Units shall be available to households earning income up to 80% of the AMI.
  29|             5.                                                                                                 Development Standards. Affordable Units shall be:
  30|                          a.                                                  Integrated with the rest of the development and shall be compatible in design,
  31|                          appearance, construction, and quality of exterior and interior materials with the other units and/or
  32|                          lots;
  33|                          b.                                                                                              Dispersed throughout the development;
  34|                          c.                                                                                            Located such that the units have equal access to shared amenities, including light and air,
  35|                          and utilities (including any bicycle storage and/or Electric Vehicle charging stations) within the
  36|                          development;

===PAGE 160=== (layout, 37 lines)
   1|                          d.                                                                   Located such that the units have equal avoidance of any potential nuisances as market-
   2|                          rate units within the development;
   3|                          e.                                                                                                   Distributed proportionately among unit sizes; and
   4|                          f.                                                                                                         Distributed proportionately across each phase of a phased development.
   5|                          g.                                                                                                                               Occupancy permits may be issued for market-rate units prior to the end of construction of
   6|                          the entire development provided that occupancy permits for Affordable Units are issued
   7|                          simultaneously on a pro rata basis.
   8|             6.                                                         Administration. The Lunenburg Housing Authority or another qualified housing entity as
   9|             designated by the Planning Board shall be responsible for administering and enforcing the requirements
  10|             in this section.

  24| § 70-5: New or Changed Positions
  25| The Personnel Committee tentatively may add new job title and descriptions to this Plan, establishing grades
  26| with minimum and maximum wage or salary brackets             ranges for the same, and reclassifying existing jobs,
  27| revising the description and the minimum and maximum wage and salary brackets ranges therefore, and such
  28| addition or reclassification to be effective only for the period from the date of such action by the Personnel
  29| Committee to the date of any vote with respect thereto adopted at a subsequent Town Meeting but in no case
  30| later than the next Annual Town Meeting unless such later date as may be specified by such vote. Any increase
  31| in wages or salaries under this section shall be effective only if funds are available for the purpose, and
  32| approved by the Finance Committee and Select Board.
  33| § 70-7: Job Descriptions and Interpretations
  34|  A. The Personnel Committee shall maintain written job descriptions of the jobs or positions in the Plan,
  35| describing the essential functions, requirements, and duties. The descriptions shall not be interpreted as either
  36| complete or restrictive and employees shall continue to perform any duties assigned by an employee’s
  37| supervisor. Job descriptions shall be reviewed, at a minimum, upon the exit of an existing employee and
  38| before the Town seeks to fill the vacancy.
  39| B. At least e                       Every three (3) years, the Personnel Committee shall review the wage and salary schedules of all
  40| positions in the Plan, and be in a position to recommend to the Select Board any action deemed desirable to
  41| maintain a fair and equitable pay level.
  42| C. Annu                        ally, the Town Manager shall make recommendations to the Select Board regarding annual cost of
  43| living increases for consideration at Annual Town Meeting.
  44| § 70-11: Transfers,             and Promotions, and Reclassifications
  45| A. Upon promotion, the employee will automatically be placed on the pay grade for the new position at the step
  46| that is closest to, but not less than, their current rate of pay, and not less than the step increase they would

===PAGE 163=== (layout, 43 lines)
   1| have achieved on their next anniversary date had they not been promoted the lowest step at which the
   2| employee would receive a pay increase. They may also receive at the time one or more step rate increases,
   3| provided the maximum for the job is not exceeded, if the Department Head recommends that qualification and
   4| performance warrant it, and the Personnel Committee approves. If the Department Head should feel that there
   5| should be a trial period before recommending the promotional step rate increase or increases, on
   6| recommendation of the Department Head, the Personnel Committee may approve any such deferred
   7| promotional increase at the conclusion of the trial period.
   8| B. If an employee is transferred to a job with a lower rate range, or rate of pay, they shall enter it at the pay rate
   9| closest to their current rate or at the maximum rate for the job, whichever is the lower.
  10| C. If an employee is reclassified to a higher grade, the employee will be placed to the higher grade at the step
  11| that is closest to, but not less than, their current rate of pay, and not less than the step increase they would
  12| have achieved on their next anniversary date had they not been reclassified.
  13| § 70-12 A.: New Personnel
  14| All employees shall be hired at the minimum of the rate range of the job for which the new employee is hired
  15| unless the Town Manager, after consultation with the Chair of the Personnel Committee, authorizes paying the
  16| employee at a higher step due to the employee’s qualifications and experience or marketing conditions. The
  17| Personnel Committee must formally vote to approve any proposal by the Town Manager to pay the new
  18| employee above Step 4. In the event that the Personnel Committee does not have enough members to conduct
  19| business, the Select Board shall have the authority to administer this provision of the Salary Administration
  20| Plan. The Town Manager may not use the provision of Section 70-                       2 paragraph G to hire a new employee
  21| above Step 4.
  22| § 70-12 D.: Special Merit Awards
  23| Special Merit Awards - In addition to pay increases which may be awarded to an employee, the Town Manager
  24| may annually make a one-time award of two hundred fifty dollars and No Cents ($250.00) to up to three
  25| employees who have gone above and beyond in one of three (3) categories. There shall be only one (1) award in
  26| each of these three (3) categories, which are:
  27| Communications: Displays a commitment to assisting the public and transparency in government including, but
  28| not limited to, improving and/or devising new ways to communicate information within the organization and to
  29| the public at large.
  30| Efficiency: Displays a commitment to ensuring we operate proficiently and efficiently by “stepping up” and
  31| “stepping in” to undertake nominal cross training in mission critical functions, exhibits a willingness to “float”
  32| as needed, and/or suggests ideas that result in ease of processing, and savings of time, material, storage
  33| requirements and the like.
  34| Pinnacle of Excellence: Displays a willingness to make extraordinary efforts in the ongoing improvement of the
  35| organization, assisting other staff members or departments to complete new or ongoing assignments and often
  36| requires the person to “stretch” to learn new computer programs, methodologies or processes.
  37| The Town Manager shall annually solicit nominations of employees from citizens at large, members of a Board,
  38| Committee, Commission, Department Heads, or fellow employees for such awards. The Town Manager shall
  39| make all determinations regarding the nominees. Nominations shall be made on a form approved by the Town
  40| Manager. All recipients will be publicly recognized for their accomplishment and have a letter of
  41| commendation placed in their personnel file in addition to their one-time award of monies.
  42| § 70-12-1: Recruitment Incentives
  43| The Town acknowledges that there may be times of extremely low unemployment, a discipline specific

===PAGE 164=== (layout, 43 lines)
   1| shortage of qualified applicants, or recruitment challenges posed by the Town’s wage structure, that the
   2| recruitment of needed employees may prove so difficult as to make it problematic to deliver certain mission
   3| critical services. Upon the Town Manager making such a finding, they may offer the prospective employee a
   4| recruitment incentive. Incentives may include, but are not limited to the by deposit                        ing of up to five (5) days of
   5| vacation leave time, which shall be charged against earned leave time over the coming year, with which to
   6| begin their employment, a one-time sign-on bonus, or other similar limited allowances.
   7| § 70-13: Grievance Procedure
   8| A. The Town will promptly consider and respond to employee grievances. The preferred method of
   9| addressing grievances is informally with the employee’s supervisor, to correct the cause of the grievance and
  10| encourage employees and supervisors to address and resolve problems as they arise. If the cause of a
  11| grievance cannot be resolved informally, the below procedure should be followed.

  24| receipt of the appeal and will respond in writing to the employee’s grievance within 30 days after meeting with
  25| the employee. The Town Manager’s decision shall be final and binding.
  26| § 70-17: Hours of Work; Overtime; Compensatory Time

  33| duly paid time off, including but not limited to holidays, sick leave, vacation, personal days and bereavement

  40| B. Exempt Employees:
  41| Exempt Employees primarily performing work that is not subject to the overtime provisions of the FLSA

  28| The amount of the monthly accrual is adjusted in December and June to adjust for rounding during

  30| B. Earned vacation time up to and including 80 hours must be used in the year granted. No unused
  31| portion of this allowance shall be carried forward into a subsequent vacation year, nor shall any
  32| monetary compensation be given for such unused portion. Earned vacation time in excess of 80 hours
  33| should be used in the year granted, and no portion of such excess shall be carried forward into a
  34| subsequent year. If departmental scheduling or other serious extenuating circumstances preclude the use
  35| of all such excess in the year granted, the employee may request to receive compensation equivalent to
  36| such unused portion in a lump sum payable on the first payroll warrant in July, in addition to their
  37| regular salary, or may be allowed to carry over such excess as the Town may elect in its sole discretion.
  38| Any employee asserting a serious extenuating circumstance must submit a written request to their direct
  39| supervisor and such request must be approved by the direct supervisor and the Town Manager before
  40| the employee shall be compensated for, or allowed to carry over, such excess.

===PAGE 166=== (layout, 45 lines)
   1| D. Employees may begin using vacation time after one full calendar month of continuous service. In order to
   2| provide flexibility, vacation time may be used before time is actually accrued, with advance written approval
   3| of the Department Head and Human Resources Director. Employees will be required to pay back any portion
   4| of unearned vacation that was paid in advance if the employee should leave the Town’s employment prior to
   5| that vacation becoming accrued. Employees may be required to sign an authorization for this deduction.
   6| E. Accruals are capped at the employee's annual accrual level, plus five (5) days. For example, if an the
   7| employee has 5 years’ service, their maximum vacation accrual would be 20 days (15 days + 5 days).
   8| Notwithstanding the prior two sentences, employees classified as part-time A will be capped at a maximum of
   9| twice the number of hours they are regularly scheduled to work in a week. Accruals shall be suspended if the
  10| employee’s vacation balance reaches the applicable cap. Accruals will resume once the balance falls below
  11| the cap.
  12| F. When an employee’s vacation accrual increases, the accrual for that month should be calculated as a
  13| weighted average of the number of calendar days at the previous accrual rate and the number of calendar
  14| days for the new accrual rate.
  15| C. G. Employment Termination. An employee whose employment ends shall be paid for all accrued, but unused
  16| vacation leave, minus any vacation time used, but not yet accrued.
  17| D. The vacation year shall begin July 1. In the first year of employment, employees shall accrue one (1)
  18| day of vacation leave (prorated based on number of hours worked each week) per month of service
  19| completed to a maximum of 80 hours to be available for use by the employee on the following July 1st.
  20| Vacation leave accrued each fiscal year will be available for use on the following July 1st. Any change in
  21| the rate of accrual shall occur on the employee’s anniversary date. When an employee’s anniversary date
  22| for the completion of the 5th, 10th-20th years occurs after July 1st, the employee shall receive vacation
  23| leave for the remainder of the year on a pro-rated basis.
  24| E. H. Vacation leave shall be approved by the Department Head and/or their designee for such time or times as
  25| best serve the public interest, provided, however, that each employee shall be entitled to use at least 40 hours of
  26| their vacation accrual during the period between June 1 and September 15 if desired, based on seniority.
  27| F. No vacation time may be used in advance of the July 1 date on which it would normally be credited;
  28| except that where such advance serves the needs of the employee and the Town, it may be granted, upon
  29| request of the employee, by the Department Head, subject to the written approval of the Town Manager.
  30| In no case shall any such advanced vacation exceed the number of days for which the employee would be
  31| entitled to compensation, were they to terminate their services in good standing on the first day of such
  32| vacation.
  33| G. I. The Town Manager,                         with the approval of the Select Board,may award a new employee an accrual rate of
  34| vacation leave in recognition of the employee’s qualifications and experience, or market conditions provided
  35| that such initial accrual shall not exceed three (3) four (4) weeks. Such employees shall be awarded a service
  36| date for the purpose of vacation leave accruals only, which shall be used for future increases in the accrual rate.
  37| J. To effectuate the transition from the prior vacation leave benefit to the accrual-based vacation leave
  38| system, any vacation time earned and unused as of July 1, 2026 shall be converted into a one-time “Vacation
  39| Bank”. Employees shall be required to use at least one-third (⅓) of their banked time during each of the
  40| following three fiscal years (FY27, FY28, FY29). Banked vacation shall be used in accordance with Town
  41| policies. All employees with a balance over 120 hours as of June 30, 2026, shall receive a lump-sum buyout
  42| of all time over 120 hours. The banked vacation shall be maintained as a separate balance and used prior to
  43| newly accrued leave (in any given fiscal year); provided employees may combine the last of their vacation
  44| leave from their Vacation Bank for a given year and accrued vacation leave from the given year to cover a
  45| single block of time.

   1| Employees may request, and the Town Manager may approve subject to the availability of funds, to be paid

   3| in three equal increments for FY ’27, FY ’28 and FY ’29 unless the employee and Town Manager agree that
   4| the banked time shall be used in a shorter period of time.

   7| § 70-19: Paid Holidays
   8| C. Holiday leave will be granted on the day the Town observes the holiday, when possible. If the holiday falls
   9| on a Saturday, it will be observed on the preceding Friday. If the holiday falls on a Sunday, it will be observed
  10| on the following Monday. If an eligible employee is required to work on the day the Town observes the holiday,
  11| they will be entitled to a Floating Day, which has to be used within 30 days the Fiscal Year                                                , by agreement of
  12| the supervisor and employee. If the department head determines that holiday leave cannot be granted, the
  13| employee shall receive payment at one and one-half times the base hourly rate for all hours worked on the
  14| holiday, in addition to his or her holiday pay. Final determination is to be made by the Town Manager.
  15| D. Call Firefighters assigned to work a Day Shift at the Fire Station on a holiday shall be paid one and one half
  16| times their hourly rate for the hours worked. For purposes of this section only, Holiday time shall be considered
  17| the calendar date of the holiday, regardless of the day of the week it falls on.
  18| D. E.            To be eligible for paid holiday leave, an employee must work his or herbe in a paid status for their                                                                   full
  19| assigned shift on his or her regularly scheduled workday before a holiday, and the next regularly scheduled
  20| working day following the holiday, unless the absence on either day is approved in accordance with the
  21| Town’s leave policies (e.g., vacation, personal, or authorized sick leave).employee has been excused for a
  22| legitimate reason by the direct supervisor.

  36|             COMMITTEE
  37|             (Submitted by the Town Manager and Assistant Town Manager/Human Resources Director)
  38|             To see if the Town will vote to amend the Code of Lunenburg, Chapter 70, entitled “Salary Administration
  39|             Plan,” as shown on a document entitled “November 18, 2025 Special Town Meeting, Article 17, Personnel
  40|             Committee” dated October 27, 2025, on file with the office of the Town Clerk, with additions thereto shown as
  41|             bold, italicized text and with deletions therefrom shown as bold and stricken-                  through; or take any other action
  42|             relative thereto.

===PAGE 169=== (layout, 50 lines)
   1| § 70-1: Purposes and Scope
   2| This by-law establishes a Salary Administration Plan, hereinafter called the “Plan”, which classifies several
   3| positions of town services into groups, establishes salary schedules, establishes so called “fringe” benefits, or
   4| “indirect pay” provisions, such as holidays and vacations with pay, sick leave, and the like., and establishes a
   5| Personnel Committee to administer the Plan, as hereinafter provided, and to represent the interest of
   6| both taxpayers and town employees.
   7| § 70-2 A.: Personnel Committee (Establishment)
   8| There is hereby established a Personnel Committee consisting of five members, each residing in the Town
   9| of Lunenburg, to be appointed by the Select Board, and each member shall serve for a term of three
  10| years; provided, however, that of the members originally appointed, one shall serve a term of one year,
  11| two for a term of two years, and two for a term of three years, as designated by the Select Board.
  12| However, nothing herein shall be deemed to prohibit the chair of the Personnel Committee from
  13| designating a member of said committee to serve as a representative of said Committee on a study
  14| committee of the Town Meeting, nor shall such service affect the tenure of said member of the Personnel
  15| Committee. If any member of the Personnel Committee shall resign or otherwise vacate the office before
  16| the expiration of their term, the successor shall be appointed by the Select Board, at their discretion, to
  17| serve for the balance of the unexpired term.
  18| § 70-2 B.: Personnel Committee (Town Employee)
  19| A Town employee may have a staff assignment to serve as a subject matter expert and non-voting
  20| member of the Personnel Committee and may be called upon from time to time to provide information
  21| requested by the Personnel Committee so that the Personnel Committee can make well informed
  22| decisions and proposals.
  23| § 70-2 C.: Personnel Committee (Structure)
  24| Said Committee shall elect its own chair and vice-                                          chair at their first meeting after June 30th of each year;
  25| and in the absence or incapacity of the chair, the vice-                                          chair shall act as chair. The Committee shall keep a
  26| record of its official proceedings and actions, may establish its own rule of procedure
  27| and may, subject to appropriation therefore, retain such clerical and other assistance, and make such
  28| other expenditures as may be necessary to the performance of its duties. Three members shall constitute
  29| a quorum for the transaction of the business of the committee, and the affirmative vote of three members
  30| shall be necessary to any official act of the Committee.
  31| § 70-2 D.: Personnel Committee (Role)
  32| The Personnel Committee is hereby authorized to administer the provisions of this by-law, except for
  33| such duties as may be specifically assigned by statute, Town Charter or by-law to other Town officers,
  34| boards or committees.
  35| § 70-2 E.: Personnel Committee (Structure)
  36| The Personnel Committee may from time to timeissue, amend, or revoke Administrative Orders for the
  37| purpose of giving effect to the provisions of this by-law, and for the purpose of giving effect to the
  38| provisions of such other by-laws and votes of the Town, pertaining to personnel administration, as said
  39| Committee may be responsible for administering and/or enforcing. Each such order shall be numbered in
  40| sequence, and said Committee shall maintain in the Town Office a file for all such orders issued, said file
  41| to be open to public inspection.
  42| § 70-2 F.: Personnel Committee (Access)
  43| Except as otherwise provided by law, the Committee shall have access to all facts, figures, records and
  44| other information relating to the personnel of Town departments, and the same shall be furnished
  45| forthwith by any such department whenever so requested by the Personnel Committee, in such a form as
  46| said Committee may require.
  47| § 70-2 G.: Personnel Committee (No Committee)
  48| In the event that the Personnel Committee does not have enough members to conduct business, the Town
  49| Manager shall have the authority to administer the Salary Administration Plan.
  50| § 70-5: New or Changed Positions

===PAGE 170=== (layout, 44 lines)
   1| The Personnel CommitteeTown Manager tentatively may add new job title and descriptions to this Plan,
   2| establishing grades with minimum and maximum wage or salary brackets for the same, and reclassifying
   3| existing jobs, revising the description and the minimum and maximum wage and salary brackets therefore, and
   4| such addition or reclassification to be effective only for the period from the date of such action by the
   5| Personnel CommitteeTown Manager to the date of any vote with respect thereto adopted at a subsequent
   6| Town Meeting but in no case later than the next Annual Town Meeting unless such later date as may be
   7| specified by such vote. Any increase in wages or salaries under this section shall be effective only if funds are
   8| available for the purpose, and approved by the Finance Committee and Select Board.
   9| § 70-6: Reclassification of Employees
  10| No employee shall be reclassified to a job in another group, either higher or lower, until the Personnel
  11| Committee Town Manager shall have determined that such a reclassification will be consistent with the
  12| provisions of the Salary Administration Plan. Eligibility for a step increase of a reclassified employee will be
  13| granted one year from the date of reclassification.
  14| § 70-7: Job Descriptions and Interpretations
  15| A. The Personnel CommitteeHuman Resources Director shall maintain written job descriptions of the jobs or
  16| positions in the Plan, describing the essential functions, requirements, and duties. The descriptions shall not be
  17| interpreted as either complete or restrictive and employees shall continue to perform any duties assigned by an
  18| employee’s supervisor.
  19| B. Every three (3) years, the Personnel CommitteeHuman Resources Director shall review the wage and
  20| salary schedules of all positions in the Plan, and be in a position to recommend to the Select Board any action
  21| deemed desirable to maintain a fair and equitable pay level.
  22| § 70-8: Salary Schedule
  23| A. The Classification and Salary Schedule of the Salary Administration Plan, set forth in Schedule A of this by-
  24| law, shall consist of the maximum and minimum salaries and step-rate salaries for the groups and positions in
  25| the Classification and Salary Schedule. The salary range of a group shall be the salary range for all positions
  26| classified in such group.
  27| B. Irrespective of the period of time for which pay rates may be shown in the Salary Schedule, all employees
  28| shall continue to be paid on an hourly, weekly, monthly, or other basis, as at present, unless otherwise
  29| authorized by the Personnel Committeeor by amendment of the Salary Administration Plan.
  30| § 70-11: Transfers and Promotions
  31| A. Upon promotion, the employee will be placed on the pay grade for the new position at the lowest step at
  32| which the employee would receive a pay increase. They may also receive at the time one or more step rate
  33| increases, provided the maximum for the job is not exceeded, if the Department Head recommends that
  34| qualification and performance warrant it, and the Personnel CommitteeTown Manager approves. If the
  35| Department Head should feel that there should be a trial period before recommending the promotional step rate
  36| increase or increases, on recommendation of the Department Head, the Personnel CommitteeTown Manager
  37| may approve any such deferred promotional increase at the conclusion of the trial period.
  38| B. If an employee is transferred to a job with a lower rate range, or rate of pay, they shall enter it at the pay rate
  39| closest to their current rate or at the maximum rate for the job, whichever is the lower.
  40| § 70-12: New Personnel
  41| All employees shall be hired at the minimum of the rate range of the job for which the new employee is hired
  42| unless the Town Manager, after consultation with the Chair of the Personnel Committee                       , authorizes paying
  43| the employee at a higher step due to the employee’s qualifications and experience or marketing conditions. The
  44| Personnel CommitteeSelect Board                                                       must formally vote to approve any proposal by the Town Manager to pay

   1| the new employee above Step 4. The Town Manager may not use the provision of Section 70-2 paragraph G to
   2| hire a new employee above Step 4.
   3| § 70-14: Department Budgets
   4| Each Department Head shall include in the annual budget request, a pay adjustment section to provide
   5| funds for anticipated pay adjustments during the ensuing year, expenditures to be made therefrom only
   6| in accordance with the Salary Administration Plan with approval of the Personnel Committee.
   7| § 70-20-1: Sick Leave Bank
   8| A sick leave bank shall be established, no later than June 30, 2025, for                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          all employees, except those in a

   2| TRUST FUND COMMISSION –ANNUAL REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025
   3| (Reporting period: July 1, 2024 –June 30, 2025)
   4| INTRODUCTION
   5| The Lunenburg Trust Fund Commission, established under Massachusetts General Law
   6| c.41 §45, submits this Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2025. This report is provided for
   7| inclusion in the Annual Town Report pursuant to M.G.L. c.40 §49.
   8| COMMISSION MEMBERSHIP (FY 2025–2026)
   9| John Bowen, Chair (elected May 17, 2025)
  10| Richard Howard, Vice‑Chair (elected May 17, 2025)
  11| Vacancy –third seat remained open through most of the fiscal year.
  12| OVERVIEW OF TRUST FUNDS
  13| The Commission oversees donor‑restricted municipal trust funds in coordination with the
  14| Town Treasurer. Funds are generally pooled for investment to promote stability,
  15| efficiency, and preservation of donor intent.
